% Arabic adds real shaping on top of RTL: harf substitutes presentation forms, so the glyphs'
% char values no longer stand for the codepoints that produced them and only gi resolves them.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[main=english, bidi=default]{babel}
\babelprovide[import]{arabic}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setmainfont{Times New Roman}
\babelfont[arabic]{rm}{Arial}
\begin{document}
Test \foreignlanguage{arabic}{العربية} end.
\end{document}
